notes: Found by testing search for the first time. Place matching is substring based (haystack.includes(token)), and search_text carried the day name, so any query token that happens to be a substring of a French day name matched. Searching Notre-Dame-de-la-Mer, a real church at Albion, produced 20 results across 16 different churches - every Notre-Dame on the island - because the token mer is inside mercredi, and only their WEDNESDAY Masses came back. Someone looking up their own parish got a list mostly of other parishes. day_of_week is now excluded from search_text: the day is filtered structurally and parsed out of the query separately, so it was never needed in the text haystack. Verified: that search now returns 5 rows at the one church; prefix search still works (cure still finds Curepipe); and 18 further search cases - day names in both languages, morning and afternoon, exact times, town and parish names - pass with zero violations. Three earlier apparent failures were my test being wrong, not the app: a Sunday search correctly includes the 81 Saturday-evening vigils, which is what fulfils the obligation. New gate check G10 fails the build if a day name ever returns to search_text. No Mass time changed: 426 rows.
